scheme_name: Remembering Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears - Organisation of Special Dedicated Programmes
description:
The scheme “Remembering Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears - Organisation of Special Dedicated Programmes” was launched by the Government of Goa in 2021. 

This initiative aims to honor and recognize the contributions of veteran tiatr artistes who have significantly impacted the cultural landscape of Goa. 

Tiatr is a unique form of musical theatre that originated in Goa and has a rich history dating back to the late 19th century. 

The scheme was introduced to preserve the legacy of these artistes and to ensure that their contributions are not forgotten. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to organize special programs dedicated to the remembrance of these artistes. 

These programs are designed to celebrate their work and to educate the younger generation about their contributions to Goan culture. 

The government aims to conduct at least four major events annually under this scheme. 

Each event will feature performances, discussions, and exhibitions that highlight the life and work of selected tiatr artistes. 

The scheme also seeks to provide a platform for emerging talent in the tiatr community. 

By doing so, it aims to promote the art form and encourage new generations to engage with it. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance for organizing these events. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹50 lakh for the first year of implementation. 

This funding will cover expenses related to venue rentals, artist honorariums, promotional materials, and other logistical costs. 

Eligibility for receiving assistance under this scheme is primarily focused on organizations and groups involved in promoting tiatr. 

These organizations must be registered under the Societies Registration Act of 1860. 

They should have a proven track record of organizing cultural events in Goa. 

The application process involves submitting a detailed proposal to the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

This proposal must outline the planned event, including the names of the artistes to be honored and the activities to be conducted. 

Applicants must also provide a budget breakdown for the proposed event. 

The application must be accompanied by documents such as the organization's registration certificate, a list of past events organized, and a letter of intent. 

The deadline for submitting applications is typically set for three months before the proposed event date. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by a committee formed by the Department of Art and Culture. 

This committee will evaluate the proposals based on their cultural significance and feasibility. 

Successful applicants will be notified within one month of the application deadline. 

The disbursement of funds will occur in two installments. 

The first installment will be released upon approval of the proposal. 

The second installment will be provided after the completion of the event, upon submission of a detailed report and utilization certificate. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

This department is responsible for promoting and preserving the cultural heritage of Goa. 

They can be contacted at their office located in Panaji, Goa. 

The contact number for the Department of Art and Culture is +91 832 222 1000. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Government of Goa to promote local arts and culture. 

It aligns with the state’s commitment to preserving its rich cultural heritage. 

The tiatr art form has been a significant part of Goan identity for over a century. 

It combines elements of drama, music, and dance, often addressing social issues and cultural themes. 

The government recognizes the need to support the artists who have dedicated their lives to this art form. 

By implementing this scheme, the government aims to ensure that the contributions of past artistes are acknowledged and celebrated. 

This initiative also serves to inspire younger artists to continue the tradition of tiatr. 

The government encourages community participation in these events to foster a sense of belonging and pride in Goan culture. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the visibility of tiatr and attract more audiences to this art form. 

In addition to honoring past artistes, the scheme will also feature workshops and training sessions for aspiring tiatr performers. 

These sessions will be conducted by experienced professionals from the tiatr community. 

The aim is to equip new artists with the skills necessary to excel in this field. 

The government will also collaborate with local educational institutions to promote tiatr as part of the curriculum. 

This will help in instilling an appreciation for this art form among students from a young age. 

The scheme is expected to create a ripple effect in the local arts community. 

By fostering a supportive environment for tiatr, the government hopes to see a resurgence in interest and participation in this cultural practice. 

The long-term goal of the scheme is to establish tiatr as a recognized cultural heritage of Goa. 

This recognition will help in attracting tourism and promoting cultural exchanges. 

The government plans to document the events and activities conducted under this scheme. 

This documentation will serve as a historical record of the contributions of tiatr artistes. 

It will also provide valuable insights for future initiatives aimed at promoting Goan culture. 

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to preserving the unique cultural identity of Goa. 

By honoring the past while promoting the future, the government aims to create a sustainable cultural ecosystem. 

The initiative is a testament to the importance of arts and culture in society. 

It recognizes that the contributions of artists are vital to the cultural fabric of the community. 

In conclusion, the “Remembering Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears - Organisation of Special Dedicated Programmes” scheme is a significant step towards preserving and promoting the tiatr art form in Goa. 

Through financial support and organized events, the government aims to honor the legacy of past artistes while inspiring future generations. 

This initiative is expected to have a lasting impact on the cultural landscape of Goa. 

It will ensure that the rich tradition of tiatr continues to thrive for years to come.
